page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.6xlarge is a compute-oriented cloud instance built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 CPU operating at 2.5 GHz with 12 physical cores and hyper-threading enabled, providing 24 dedicated vCPUs. The instance features 48.0 GB of system memory, corresponding to 2.0 GB per vCPU. No local SSD storage or GPU accelerators are included with this instance type. Baseline network performance is rated at 4 Gbps.

Hardware benchmark results demonstrate moderate multi-threaded performance alongside lower single-core execution speeds. Single-core performance metrics, such as a Geekbench score of 945.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1108.08, fall into the lower quartile. However, multi-core tasks achieve solid mid-range performance, reflected by a multi-core Geekbench score of 7148.0, a PassMark CPU score of 18444.17, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 83.08 GB/sec. Uncached memory read and write bandwidths measure 90.83 GB/sec and 52.97 GB/sec, respectively.

From a qualitative efficiency perspective, the ecs.sn1ne.6xlarge provides high multi-threaded vCPU capacity relative to its memory footprint. However, its processor exhibits weak single-thread performance, posing a tradeoff for single-core bottlenecked tasks. The instance delivers steady performance in Redis operations at 16.86 million SET ops/sec and static web serving at 10.88 GB/sec. It is suitable for multi-threaded batch jobs, software compilation, web application backends, and parallel database services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.6xlarge is a compute-focused x86_64 server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor at 2.5 GHz, it features 12 physical cores and 24 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled, alongside 48.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a 4 Gbps baseline network capacity. It does not include local disk storage or GPU acceleration. Benchmarks highlight an execution profile characterized by weak single-core speeds but average multi-core processing throughput, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 18444.17 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 7148.0. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 90.83 GB/sec for reads and 52.97 GB/sec for writes. The instance offers reliable resource density for parallelized computational workloads, software compilation, static web serving, and distributed database services where high single-threaded clock speed is not required.
